title: Top 275 PDF: Words 26 to 50
subtitle: Propitious to Imperious (SSC CGL 2026 Digital Notes)

words.meaning: Giving or indicating a good chance of success; favorable.
words.example: The weather was propitious for starting the expedition.

words.meaning: Tending to obstruct or harm; unfriendly or hostile.
words.example: Excessive stress is inimical to good health.

words.meaning: Expressing or conveying a threat; menacing.
words.example: He received a minatory letter from his rivals.

words.meaning: Lacking a plan, purpose, or enthusiasm; irregular.
words.example: A desultory preparation never yields top ranks.

words.meaning: Naive, simplistic, and superficial; dry and uninteresting.
words.example: The insipid speech bored everyone in the hall.

words.meaning: Vigorous or incisive in expression or style; sharp.
words.example: She made a trenchant critique of the outdated policy.

words.meaning: Slow to act; intended to cause delay.
words.example: The office used dilatory tactics to delay the file.

words.meaning: Apparently attractive but having in reality no value or integrity.
words.example: Don't be fooled by meretricious advertisements.

words.meaning: Carried out with a minimum of effort or reflection.
words.example: He gave the document only a perfunctory glance.

words.meaning: Showing a casual lack of concern; indifferent and carefree.
words.example: He walked into the exam hall with an insouciant smile.

words.meaning: Having an obstinately uncooperative attitude toward authority.
words.example: The recalcitrant player was suspended by the board.

words.meaning: Having or showing a sharp or critical quality; biting.
words.example: The cartoonist is known for his mordant humor.

words.meaning: Showing great attention to detail or correct behavior.
words.example: He was punctilious about arriving on time every day.

words.meaning: Not having or showing foresight; spendthrift or thoughtless.
words.example: His improvident habits left him broke within a month.

words.meaning: Recklessly bold or rash; careless of danger.
words.example: Driving at high speed in fog is a temerarious act.

words.meaning: Recklessly extravagant or wasteful in the use of resources; licentious.
words.example: The profligate prince wasted the royal treasury.

words.meaning: Sentimental in a feeble or sickly way.
words.example: The movie ended with a mawkish and predictable scene.

words.meaning: Having or showing a tendency to be easily angered.
words.example: The irascible manager shouted at the staff over a small typo.

words.meaning: Having many syllables; using long words.
words.example: Avoid sesquipedalian words when simple ones work better.

words.meaning: Having great power or influence; mighty.
words.example: The puissant ruler expanded his empire across the continent.

words.meaning: Bitter and abusive in language.
words.example: The debate turned into a vituperative argument.

words.meaning: Tediously pompous or bombastic in speech or writing; swollen.
words.example: His turgid prose made the article hard to read.

words.meaning: Rude in a mean-spirited and surly way.
words.example: It would be churlish to refuse such a generous invitation.

words.meaning: Holding firmly to an opinion or a course of action.
words.example: Her pertinacious effort finally solved the mystery.

words.meaning: Assuming power or authority without justification; arrogant and domineering.
words.example: She dismissed the clerk with an imperious wave of her hand.
